tables.note: * OP nicotinic effects can give tachycardia, hypertension and dilated pupils. Features: HOSP 19.20, 19.30, 19.37 · PAED 18.5, 18.15, 18.17, 18.22, 18.24. Serotonin: clonus, hyperreflexia (Hunter card) †.

formulas.name: OP adult
formulas.expr: atropine 2 mg IV, double every 3–5 min until atropinised; then 10–20 % of total bolus per h

formulas.name: OP child
formulas.expr: atropine 0.05 mg/kg IV over 1 min, double every 3–5 min; then infusion

formulas.name: Naloxone adult
formulas.expr: 0.4 mg IV, ↑ 0.8 → 2 → 4 mg every 2–3 min (max 10 mg); infusion 0.4 mg/h

formulas.name: Naloxone child
formulas.expr: 0.1 mg/kg IV; infusion 0.01 mg/kg/h; observe ≥ 12 h

formulas.name: Agitation / seizures (anticholinergic, sympathomimetic)
formulas.expr: diazepam 0.1–0.2 mg/kg IV/PO (child); adult per status protocol

interpretation_stg.t: Atropinised = dry chest, HR ↑, BP ↑, dry skin (pupils late) — chest, not pupils, is the target
Opioid: ventilate first (bag-mask); naloxone lasts shorter than most opioids
Cocaine: benzodiazepines; no phenytoin; no β-blockers (except labetalol)
Benzodiazepine OD: supportive; flumazenil not recommended

notes.t: OP: PPE, strip and wash; notifiable
OP intermediate syndrome day 1–4: watch neck flexors
Dry skin separates anticholinergic from sympathomimetic
Charcoal adult 50 g · child < 6 y 1 g/kg
